### [1] [RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20628)
*Renbiao Jin,Mingxin Yang,Yutian Chen,Junhao Zhuang,Xin Cai,Mulin Yu,Linning Xu,Wenxian Yu,Danping Zou,Shi Guo,Tianfan Xue*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RealVDeblur proposes an efficient, robust video deblurring pipeline for real-world videos by combining physically grounded blur synthesis from 3D Gaussian Splatting and a frame-wise video diffusion prior, culminating in a one-step generator with a Temporal Window Mask for long videos, achieving superior perceptual/semantic/temporal quality and better downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world video deblurring suffers from diverse blur patterns and limited realistic training data; a realistic data synthesis pipeline and strong priors are needed for robustness and practical deployment.

Method: 1) Build large-scale blur synthesis from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting assets and high-FPS videos to capture camera and object motion blur. 2) Use a video diffusion prior with frame-wise encoding (disable temporal compression in VAE) to handle frame-dependent blur variations. 3) Distill multi-step diffusion into a one-step generator for efficiency. 4) Introduce training-free Temporal Window Mask to stabilize inference for long videos with constant memory usage.

Result: Extensive experiments show strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen real videos; improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe blur.

Conclusion: RealVDeblur offers an efficient, robust framework for in-the-wild video deblurring, enabling practical deployment and benefiting downstream tasks; the approach combines realistic data synthesis with diffusion priors and memory-efficient inference.

Abstract: Real-world video deblurring remains challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and the scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream pipelines such as mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction. This work presents \textbf{RealVDeblur}, an efficient generative framework designed to improve in-the-wild robustness under diverse real capture conditions. First, a large-scale, physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline is constructed from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos, providing realistic training data covering both camera-induced and object-motion blur. Second, a video diffusion prior is leveraged for restoration; to better accommodate frame-dependent blur variations, temporal compression in the VAE is disabled and a frame-wise encoding scheme is adopted. For practical deployment on long videos, multi-step diffusion sampling is distilled into an efficient one-step generator, and a training-free Temporal Window Mask stabilizes inference beyond the training horizon with constant memory usage. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, as well as improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur. Project page: https://rbjin.github.io/RealVDeblur

</details>


### [2] [Masked Topology Modeling for Self-Supervised Learning on Parametric CAD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20642)
*Heinrich Jiang,Jennifer Jang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A self-supervised pretraining framework for B-Rep CAD using Masked Topology Modeling (MTM) on face-adjacency graphs, combined with MoCo-style contrastive learning and region reconstruction; evaluated on ABC and a procedural dataset with strong downstream performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address data scarcity of editable B-Rep CAD data; exploit unique topology (face-adjacency graph) for graph-based pretraining to improve data efficiency and generalization in CAD tasks.

Method: MTM masks edges in the B-Rep face-adjacency graph; a small head predicts the masked edge's convexity and curve type from encoder's post-message-passing face features. Training also includes MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-Rep-aware augmentations and a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective. Pretraining on ABC dataset and a procedurally generated dataset.

Result: Demonstrates strong performance on multiple CAD benchmarks; ablations show contributions of MTM, contrastive learning, and region reconstruction; improved data efficiency and generalization.

Conclusion: MTM-based self-supervised pretraining yields domain-specific representations for editable B-Rep CAD with potential to reduce data requirements and support downstream tasks; the combination of topology-aware masking, contrastive learning, and region-based reconstruction is effective.

Abstract: Computer aided design (CAD) is ubiquitous: virtually any modern object was designed using editable CAD tools. However, with the shortage of available CAD datasets in its native editable and parametric format, boundary representation (B-Rep), it is ever more important to develop data-efficient methods for this domain.
  We present a new self-supervised pretraining task, Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), that leverages the face-adjacency graph, an induced structure unique to B-reps that the encoder can be asked to reconstruct. MTM masks a fraction of edges and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from the encoder's post-message-passing face features.
  We combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations, a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective, and pretraining on the ABC dataset and our new procedurally generated dataset to show strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

</details>


### [3] [Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20660)
*Anita Hu,Maria Shugrina*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Axolotl3D introduces a unified, multi-modal diffusion-based 3D generator that conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and partial point clouds to enable occlusion-aware, multi-view-consistent 3D completion and editing, achieving state-of-the-art results on Toys4K and OmniObject3D.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current 3D generation methods largely rely on complete visibility and single-view inputs, failing under occlusion, multi-view, or editing scenarios. There is a need for a unified framework that can coherently integrate diverse conditioning signals to enable robust, controllable 3D completion.

Method: A diffusion-based 3D generator that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The partial point cloud acts as a geometric anchor; camera parameters enforce multi-view alignment in a shared 3D space. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data to enable robust cross-modal reasoning.

Result: The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on Toys4K and OmniObject3D under both clean and occluded settings, with strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

Conclusion: Axolotl3D provides a unified, controllable 3D completion framework that integrates multiple conditioning signals to handle occlusion and multi-view constraints, enabling robust reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing across diverse scenarios.

Abstract: Recent 3D generative models produce high-quality geometry from a single image using large-scale priors and diffusion architectures. However, they assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Although prior works address these challenges individually, they lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals. We present Axolotl3D, a multi-modal and occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor promoting faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data, enabling robust cross-modal reasoning. Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, as well as strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

</details>


### [4] [ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20670)
*Yordanka Velikova,Mahdi Saleh,Liming Kuang,Benjamin Busam*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ODeform uses Neural ODEs to model continuous 4D deformation of 3D objects by embedding point clouds and material properties into a latent space and solving ODEs over time, enabling continuous, real-time deformation without discrete steps.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a need for real-time, continuous deformation modeling that avoids discrete time stepping and expensive physics simulations, suitable for manipulation, simulation, and robotics tasks.

Method: Extend Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to a continuous-time, latent-space dynamics model. Map 3D point clouds and physical properties into a unified latent representation; model deformation as continuous flows by solving the latent-space ODEs over time; demonstrate transfer to unseen shapes and parameters with interpolation/extrapolation.

Result: Outperforms baselines in motion prediction on unseen physical parameters; demonstrates transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes; shows effective interpolation and extrapolation of learned dynamics; code and data will be released.

Conclusion: Continuous-time deformation modeling via Neural ODEs provides accurate, efficient, and generalizable 4D dynamics for deformable objects, enabling real-time applications and broader adoption.

Abstract: Modeling continuous object deformation is important for many computer vision and robotics tasks, such as manipulation and simulation. Existing approaches rely on learning-based methods or physics simulators to model shape deformations. However, these approaches either use discrete time steps or are too computationally intensive for real-time applications. We present ODeform, a novel extension of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space. Our method transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions (like material properties) into a unified latent space. By solving the resulting ordinary differential equations over time, we model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating the need for discrete time steps while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on unseen physical parameter configurations, showing improved motion prediction accuracy over baseline methods. Our experiments further demonstrate a successful transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes, along with effective interpolation and extrapolation of the learned dynamics. Our code and data will be made publicly available.

</details>


### [5] [Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20691)
*Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy,Dunren Che,Haitham Y. Adarbah,Afzel Noore*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) uses coarse lesion delineations to guide concept evidence in breast ultrasound, improving diagnostic performance and spatial faithfulness, with trustworthiness validation via supervision-quality stress tests.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: CBMs offer interpretable predictions but concept activations can be influenced by irrelevant regions, leading to unfaithful explanations. Leveraging weak, anatomically grounded supervision aims to produce more faithful concept evidence in medical imaging.

Method: Use coarse lesion masks to define two zones per lesion: (i) in-lesion ROI for morphology concepts and (ii) posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. Train concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective and keep semantic fidelity with a linear bottleneck classifier.

Result: Five-fold stratified group cross-validation shows SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC, with markedly better spatial alignment of concept evidence. A train-corrupt/test-clean annotation-quality stress test quantifies the impact of supervision quality on both diagnosis and spatial faithfulness.

Conclusion: Data-quality-aware supervision and systematic trustworthiness validation are essential for deployable healthcare AI systems.

Abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models provide interpretable-by-design predictions by mediating diagnosis through human-understandable concepts, but in medical imaging, their trustworthiness is often limited by the quality and granularity of available supervision. In particular, predicted concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, leading to spatially unfaithful explanations. We study a data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) that leverages coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to encourage anatomically plausible concept evidence. For breast ultrasound, we derive two clinically motivated zones from each lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion region of interest for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. We train concept maps using a grouped spatial grounding objective and preserve semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the proposed SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. We also perform a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to quantify the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness. Overall, the results underscore the need for data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation for deployable healthcare AI systems.

</details>


### [6] [DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20692)
*Eric Regina,Richard Arnaud,Samir Hadi Cisneros*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slices using Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with a post-generation Supervisor that filters candidates via autoencoder embeddings, DPPs, and Stein Kernel Thinning. It achieves a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and FID of 0.3290, showing a strong realism-privacy trade-off, but deeper patient-specific identity leakage persists despite filtering.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Tackle privacy risks in synthetic medical imaging by balancing realism and privacy; current approaches reduce memorization but may not fully prevent patient re-identification.

Method: 1) Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM) for synthesis; 2) privacy-oriented training; 3) a post-generation Supervisor pipeline that filters candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings; 4) diversity and thinning via Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs) and Stein Kernel Thinning.

Result: Best model achieves Privacy Preservation Score = 0.549 and FID = 0.3290. Geometric filtering reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage; however, patient re-identification scores remain, indicating that direct image copying is not the sole source of privacy risk.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a notable realism-privacy trade-off in privacy-preserving medical image generation. While geometric filtering mitigates several leakage channels, deeper patient-specific anatomical identity remains vulnerable, outlining a key area for future work in stronger de-identification and privacy auditing.

Abstract: We present a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge. The approach combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline that filters generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning. Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off, with the best-performing model achieving a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and competitive visual fidelity with an FID of 0.3290. While the proposed geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, highlighting an important frontier for future privacy-preserving medical image generation.

</details>


### [7] [U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20705)
*Elijah Danquah Darko,Min Xian,Terence Soule,Tiankai Yao,Matthew William Anderson*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score and pseudo-clicks to guide a cascade of refinement steps in interactive image segmentation, using a dual-head network; achieves >10% reduction in required manual clicks on Berkeley and improves boundary accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reduce annotation effort and speed up interactive segmentation by enabling autonomous self-correction after each user interaction, addressing the inefficiency of many corrective clicks and slow convergence in existing methods.

Method: A boundary-aware uncertainty score fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to place internal pseudo-clicks at the most ambiguous boundary regions. A dual-head encoder-decoder network (segmentation head for region consistency; edge head for sharper boundaries) supports the refinement. Inference runs a cascade of refinement stages where each stage uses these uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to progressively refine the mask.

Result: Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved click efficiency, better initial mask quality, and enhanced boundary accuracy. The approach reduces required clicks by over 10% on Berkeley and demonstrates more intelligent, efficient interactive annotation.

Conclusion: U-CFR demonstrates that autonomy in self-correction during interactive segmentation is effective, yielding notable gains in efficiency and boundary accuracy, particularly on challenging datasets.

Abstract: Interactive image segmentation is critical for efficient image annotation; however, existing methods often require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly. We propose Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR), a novel inference-time framework that enables models to autonomously self-correct after each user interaction. U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to guide the placement of internal pseudo-clicks. These self-generated clicks target the most ambiguous boundary regions, providing strong corrective signals without additional manual input. To support this process, we design a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder backbone: a segmentation head ensures region consistency, while an edge head sharpens boundary alignment. In inference, U-CFR launches a cascade of refinement steps, where each stage leverages the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to refine the mask progressively. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed U-CFR improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy. It reduces the required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley and offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

</details>


### [8] [Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20780)
*Inpyo Song,Jangwon Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) evaluation conflates conditional abnormality definitions with generic anomaly signals (definition blindness). The paper introduces definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ) and a definition-contrastive score (DeCoS) to isolate and quantify definition-sensitive anomaly scoring, showing improved cross-definition discrimination across UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current VAD and OWVAD evaluations fail to isolate the conditional behavior of OWVAD, where changing the user-defined abnormality definition should alter which moments are labeled anomalous. Standard metrics can be driven by target-vs-normal separation, masking the model's ability to adapt to definitions.

Method: 1) Decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-vs-normal detection and target-vs-other-anomaly discrimination; 2) propose three definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ) that progressively remove shortcuts from normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection; 3) introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence common across definitions; 4) empirical evaluation on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, MSAD with leading VAD, OWVAD, and vision-language model baselines.

Result: Findings show that target-vs-normal detection receives the majority (7.2–26.8×) of weight in common benchmarks, indicating definition blindness. DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ mitigate shortcuts, and DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3–16.0 AUROC on DC-Disc and 15.5–28.3 AUROC on DC-DetΔ across datasets.

Conclusion: OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring rather than generic anomaly detection with varying prompts; the proposed metrics and DeCoS provide a more faithful assessment of a model’s ability to follow user-defined definitions.

Abstract: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) is expected to detect events that match a user-specified definition of abnormality. This requirement is stronger than generic anomaly localization: in the same video, changing the definition should change which temporal regions are scored as anomalous. We show that current OWVAD evaluation largely fails to isolate this conditional behavior. Standard VAD metrics and the dynamic-definition protocol can be dominated by target-versus-normal separation, allowing models to obtain strong scores while remaining nearly insensitive to the queried definition. We call this failure mode definition blindness. To explain why it is missed, we decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination, and find that the former receives 7.2-26.8$\times$ more weight across common VAD benchmarks. Motivated by this diagnosis, we introduce three definition-conditioned evaluation metrics, DC-Disc, DC-Det$Δ$, and DC-Sel$Δ$, which progressively remove normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection shortcuts. Experiments on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD reveal that several strong VAD, OWVAD, and general vision language model baselines localize anomalous moments but exhibit weak definition following, often with near-zero definition-response margins. To validate that the failure is actionable, we further introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC points on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 points on DC-Det$Δ$. Overall, our results argue that OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

</details>


### [9] [3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20789)
*Xuening Tian,Dieter Schmalstieg,Shohei Mori*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A fast, 3D-consistent object removal framework for Gaussian splatting that uses a single-view inpainting as an appearance prior and 3D-aware PatchMatch to propagate textures across views, improving speed and view consistency over multi-view diffusion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Diffusion-based iterative 3D editing methods are computationally heavy and prone to hallucination drift, causing multi-view inconsistencies and artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints.

Method: 1) Perform a single generative inpainting on a key reference view to establish an appearance prior; 2) Apply a 3D-aware PatchMatch to propagate reference textures to other views via correspondences, bypassing diffusion; 3) Favor reconstructive consistency to maintain high-frequency details within 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Result: Competitive inpainting quality relative to diffusion methods across views; superior rendering speed and view consistency; preservation of high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions; yields a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction.

Conclusion: 3D-GIMP offers a hybrid approach that achieves high-fidelity object removal with improved speed and consistency in 3D Gaussian Splatting, validating the trade-off between reconstructive consistency and iterative generation; shows potential for broader 3D editing tasks.

Abstract: Recent advances in 3D scene editing have leveraged iterative diffusion models to update input views. However, this process is computationally expensive and struggles to produce sharp details. Meanwhile, ``hallucination drift'' frequently introduces multi-view inconsistencies, leading to structural artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints. To address this problem, we present 3D-GIMP (3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets Patch Matching), a novel hybrid paradigm designed for high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of diffusing every view, 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, which serves as an appearance prior. We then introduce a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate these reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, effectively bypassing the stochastic nature of frame-by-frame diffusion. By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP maintains high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions while ensuring a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction. Our experiments demonstrate that 3D-GIMP not only achieves competitive inpainting quality as previous methods using diffusion in multiple views, but also outperforms these methods in rendering speed and view consistency.

</details>


### [10] [Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20790)
*Husanpreet Singh,Robert Tran,Ayushree Kharel,Sudipta Banerjee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: VR iris recognition in unconstrained VR data: evaluate ISO/IEC 29794-6 quality metrics on VRBiom, address data-specific issues with generative models, and compare unimodal iris vs periocular vs multimodal fusion; fusion yields ~11% EER reduction; will release evaluation scripts.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Enhance reliability of biometric authentication for VR headsets by confronting off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflections, and by evaluating the relevance of existing iris quality metrics on VR data.

Method: 1) Evaluate ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on the VRBiom VR iris dataset and analyze limitations. 2) Mitigate data-specific challenges (off-axis gaze, illumination non-uniformity, specular reflections) using generative models to synthesize/repair images. 3) Conduct unimodal iris and periocular recognition; perform score-level fusion iris+periocular; compare to unimodal iris.

Result: Some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data. Image adjustments mainly benefit periocular recognition. Multimodal fusion lowers EER by approximately 11% relative to unimodal iris recognition.

Conclusion: Existing iris quality metrics may not transfer directly to VR data; generative-model-based corrections can address VR-specific artefacts; multimodal (iris + periocular) recognition provides measurable gains; reproducibility will be facilitated by releasing evaluation scripts.

Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) headsets (e.g., Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro) provide a seamless user experience due to their fast, frictionless interaction with the physical world in a simulated environment. User authentication relies on biometric cues such as iris in such headsets. However, traditional iris recognition protocols may not be adequate in cases of unconstrained acquisition, which is typical of VR-based data. In this work, we examine three crucial aspects: (1) evaluating ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset and analyzing their limitations, (2) addressing data-specific challenges such as off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection using generative models, and (3) performing unimodal (iris, periocular) recognition and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular). We observe that some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; whereas, image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition performance. We will release the evaluation scripts upon acceptance for reproducibility.

</details>


### [11] [SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20813)
*Jiun Lee,Jaekwang Kim,Sangmin Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SubSplat proposes Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, enhancing structural density from low-resolution features while using feature aggregation to capture high-frequency details across views, aiming to overcome the input-resolution vs. computational-cost trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting; evaluated on RealEstate10K and ACID with reported high fidelity and efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The method addresses a core trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting: increasing input resolution yields higher detail but incurs quadratically higher network computation, while low-resolution inputs reduce cost but degrade density and introduce artifacts. SubSplat seeks to maintain density and detail without prohibitive cost.

Method: Introduce Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide each primary Gaussian into finer primitives, effectively increasing density directly from low-resolution features. Enhance reparameterization with feature aggregation across multiple views to better capture high-frequency details.

Result: Empirical results on RealEstate10K and ACID show SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency, indicating the proposed SPGR-based density restoration and view-aggregation strategy successfully mitigates the input-resolution vs. compute trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting.

Conclusion: SubSplat provides a framework that reconciles reparameterization fidelity with network computational cost in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting, enabling high-quality novel-view synthesis at reduced computational overhead.

Abstract: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting enables efficient and generalizable novel-view synthesis. However, high-resolution rendering faces a critical trade-off where increasing input resolution improves detail at the expense of quadratically rising network computational cost. Conversely, maintaining low-resolution inputs stabilizes this cost but results in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. To address this, we propose SubSplat, which introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer(SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density directly from low-resolution features. We further enhance the reparameterization quality through feature aggregation, which effectively captures high-frequency details across multiple views. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency. Our results validate that the proposed framework successfully resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting.

</details>


### [12] [Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20819)
*Thomas Kassiotis,Stefanos Gkikas,Nikolaos Smyrnis,Giorgos Giannakakis*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: StressGAT: a graph attention network with differential action units and MIL for personalized, interpretable stress recognition via LOSO; achieves 88.62% accuracy on 58-participant cohort.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses substantial inter-individual variability in facial stress expressions and the limitations of traditional RNN/CNN architectures that overlook person-specific baselines, suffer from sequential bottlenecks, rigid grid constraints, and limited interpretability for clinical deployment.

Method: Employs StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages relational inductive bias to model facial dynamics; uses Differential Action Units to normalize responses relative to neutral baselines; incorporates a Multiple Instance Learning attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal expressivity phenotypes; evaluated under subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation.

Result: Achieves 88.62% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort of 58 participants with LOSO validation; MIL attention enables localization of peak stress intervals and characterization of expressivity phenotypes.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a robust, interpretable, personalized framework for affective monitoring that combines relational graph modeling, baseline normalization, and MIL-based interpretability to support clinical deployment.

Abstract: Stress is a dynamic process characterized by significant individual variability in facial expression. Traditional architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often overlook person-specific baselines or lack the representational capacity to model the non-linear temporal progression of distress due to sequential bottlenecks and rigid grid-based constraints. Furthermore, many deep learning models lack the interpretability required for clinical deployment. This study introduces StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages the relational inductive bias of graph modeling to capture complex facial dynamics that indicate acute stress. By using Differential Action Units, the framework normalizes individual responses relative to neutral baselines to achieve personalized recognition. The proposed model achieves 88.62\% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort (58 participants) using a subject-independent, Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation protocol. Beyond predictive accuracy, the architecture integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal distinct expressivity phenotypes. By simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability, this framework provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring.

</details>


### [13] [Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20866)
*Zhijing Yang,Haocheng Lin,Zhihua Xu,Haojie Li,Keze Wang,Liang Lin,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A modular multi-agent framework for structure-aware interior layout generation with a progressive proposal-evaluation-refinement loop, plus a structure-centric benchmark.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address failures of one-shot generation methods to verify intermediate geometric constraints, preventing collisions and infeasible layouts under complex room constraints.

Method: Three agents (Generator, Evaluator, Refiner) operate under a Progressive Consensus Mechanism that enforces stepwise geometric validation before placement; InStruct benchmark with 18k annotated samples and new metrics.

Result: Significant improvements over state-of-the-art in strict structural adherence and functional coherence; qualitative analyses and user studies corroborate; robust dataset and metrics.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a viable, scalable approach to constraint-aware layout synthesis and standardized evaluation, with potential extensions to broader spatial-design tasks.

Abstract: Generating realistic interior furniture layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints (e.g., walls, doors, and windows) remains a fundamental challenge in automated spatial design. Existing approaches, primarily based on one-shot generation using diffusion models or Large Language Models (LLMs), lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, often resulting in structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints. To address these challenges, we propose Agentic Designer, a progressive, multi-agent framework that formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative and constraint-verified decision process. By decomposing layout synthesis into modular stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, the framework coordinates three specialized agents, a Generator, an Evaluator, and a Refiner, through a Progressive Consensus Mechanism. This mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, thereby preventing error accumulation. To facilitate this structure-aware paradigm and standardize evaluation, we establish InStruct, a comprehensive benchmark that integrates a dataset comprising over 18,000 high-quality, parametrically annotated samples with a novel suite of structure-centric metrics. Extensive quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies show that Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

</details>


### [14] [ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20868)
*Han Li,Si Liu,Zehao Huang,Dongxin Lyu,Longfei Xu,Jiahui Fu,Daxin Tian,Yuliang Xiu,Naiyan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ViSTR-Bench offers a qualitative four-dimensional benchmark to evaluate visual spatial-temporal reasoning in dynamic scenes, revealing substantial gaps in current MLLMs' intuitive understanding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the gap between strong general video understanding and human-like temporal-spatial reasoning, by focusing on qualitative reasoning from temporal cues rather than static scenes or exact predictions.

Method: Four-dimension framework with Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics; 15 subtasks; 1,340 video QA pairs across tabletop, indoor, and outdoor settings; emphasizes temporal cues and qualitative evaluation; evaluated across diverse model families (proprietary, open-source, specialized spatial MLLMs).

Result: Finds that state-of-the-art spatial MLLMs exhibit substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and perform far below human baselines despite strong video understanding capabilities.

Conclusion: ViSTR-Bench provides a comprehensive, scalable evaluation for qualitative temporal reasoning in MLLMs and underscores the need for models capable of integrating continuous visual cues; results set a new benchmark for future improvements in spatio-temporal reasoning.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse expert-level tasks, but they still struggle with fundamental abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous observation of the real world, such as spatial perception and dynamic reasoning. Recent studies have recognized this gap and introduced dedicated benchmarks to evaluate the spatial-temporal capabilities of MLLMs. However, existing benchmarks mostly focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues largely underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Visual Spatial-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark (ViSTR-Bench), a novel evaluation suite designed to systematically assess whether MLLMs can perform qualitative reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes. Guided by the principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation, ViSTR-Bench establishes a comprehensive four-dimensional evaluations covering Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics. The benchmark comprises 15 distinct subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video question-answer pairs spanning diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios. Extensive evaluations of a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs reveal that, despite their strong general video understanding capabilities, current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

</details>


### [15] [Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20874)
*Zhihua Xu,Zhijing Yang,Yufeng Yang,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes a webly supervised multi-label benchmark (WS-MLR) with Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) method that learns category-specific instance- and category-level representations to identify/correct noisy labels, achieving superior performance over baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Webly supervised learning is well-studied for single-label tasks, but multi-label web supervision lacks unified benchmarks and fair evaluation protocols. A benchmark and robust method are needed to advance the field and enable fair comparisons.

Method: Construct WS-MLR benchmark by collecting Web-COCO and Web-Pascal datasets (~300k images, 80/20 categories matching MS-COCO/Pascal VOC) with category-word search keywords; re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting; propose Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) that jointly learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations and their cross-level similarities to identify and correct noisy labels.

Result: Extensive experiments on the benchmark show that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared with representative baselines.

Conclusion: WS-MLR provides a unified, scalable benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition; DBMLCL offers effective noise-robust learning by leveraging dual-branch category-specific representations, demonstrating strong empirical gains.

Abstract: Training deep learning models with freely available web images can reduce their dependence on costly manual annotations. Although webly supervised learning has been widely studied for single-label recognition, its multi-label counterpart remains underexplored, partly due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols. To address this gap, we construct a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR), including Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting. The two datasets cover the same 80 and 20 categories as MS-COCO and Pascal VOC, respectively, and contain about 300 thousand images retrieved from the Internet using category-word combinations as search keywords. We further propose a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework, which learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations together with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels. Extensive experiments on the benchmark demonstrate that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines.

</details>


### [16] [WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20883)
*Ming Hu,Mingyu Dou,Jianfu Yin,Miaomiao Zhang,Cong Hu,Yao Wang,Bingliang Hu,Quan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: WhereEdit reframes one-step text-to-image editing as localized adaptive editing by identifying semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applying region-specific modulation. This yields stronger local edits while preserving non-target regions, achieving state-of-the-art results on PIE-Bench with maintained one-step efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing one-step T2I editing methods rely on text conditioning and often perform global semantic transport, lacking explicit spatial control. This limits high-intensity, localized edits and stable region-specific transformations.

Method: Introduce WhereEdit, a framework that automatically identifies target regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to those regions. It preserves non-target areas and structural consistency, reformulating editing as localized, region-aware manipulation within a one-step generation framework.

Result: On the PIE-Bench benchmark, WhereEdit consistently outperforms prior one-step editing methods in editing quality while maintaining one-step generation efficiency. Region-level supervision experiments further demonstrate the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality localized edits.

Conclusion: Spatially controlled one-step editing is feasible and advantageous. By leveraging internal features to locate editable regions and applying adaptive local modulation, WhereEdit achieves superior local edits without sacrificing efficiency, with explicit region-level supervision reinforcing the value of spatial reasoning.

Abstract: Recent one-step text-to-image (T2I) models enable efficient image synthesis and provide new opportunities for real-time image editing. However, existing one-step editing methods primarily rely on text conditioning for semantic transformation, lacking explicit spatial control over \textit{where} to edit. More importantly, even when spatial constraints are introduced, these methods often struggle to achieve strong and stable semantic modifications within the target regions. In this work, we revisit one-step image editing from a spatially controlled perspective and identify two key challenges: discovering editable regions and achieving effective localized semantic transformation. We reveal that existing methods perform global semantic transport, which limits high-intensity local editing under the one-step setting. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{WhereEdit}, a framework that reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing. WhereEdit automatically identifies semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency. Experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark demonstrate that WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining the efficiency of one-step generation. Additional experiments with region-level supervision further highlight the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step image editing.

</details>


### [17] [Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20889)
*Junhao Chen,Xinghao Chen,Henghaofan Zhang,Zihao Qiao,Saining Zhang,Yongzhi Li,Ruqi Huang,Sisi Li,Yimin Sheng,Jianyi Zhu,Hao Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Lumera: a benchmark and pipeline for single-image, engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing; introduces Lumera-2K dataset; demonstrates Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light with strong detection/geometry but weaker light localization; identifies bottlenecks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Enable editable, engine-native 3D scenes with inspectable objects and lights from a single image; address limitations of prior single-image methods that stop at room-scale or baked GI.

Method: Build Lumera-2K from 2,513 UE5 projects; assemble 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K parametric lights, 95.1K camera views. Adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I) and reconstruct per-object meshes, estimate HDR environment, run bounded agentic refinement.

Result: Lumera-Box achieves best overall detection, geometry, semantic, layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762); anchor recall higher for WildDet3D. Lumera-Light achieves recall 0.998 on non-empty scenes; but light localization is weak (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median pos error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, intensity r=0.628.

Conclusion: Parametric lights are a measurable editable-scene target; remaining bottlenecks include relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

Abstract: Editable 3D scene creation requires object instances and lights that can be inspected, moved, and imported into standard engines, yet existing single-image methods largely stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation. We introduce Lumera (Light-aware Unified Engine-native Reconstruction and Assembly), a benchmark and reference pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing from a single image. Lumera-2K is built from 2,513 UE5 projects and provides 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views. On this data, Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I), which are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. In a sanitized box benchmark against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D, Lumera-Box obtains the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762), while WildDet3D remains stronger on anchor recall. For lights, Lumera-Light recovers almost all non-empty scenes (recall 0.998) but remains limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, and intensity Pearson r=0.628. These results establish parametric lights as a measurable editable-scene target and expose remaining bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

</details>


### [18] [MAGE-Vein: Multi-Instance Age and Gender Estimation from Finger Vein Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20897)
*Katsuki Tanaka,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki,Masakazu Fujio,Yosuke Kaga,Kanade Oshima,Kenta Takahashi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MAGE-Vein uses multi-instance multi-task learning on three-finger finger vein images with hybrid feature-level fusion and gender conditioning to estimate age, achieving MAE 6.12 years and r=0.880 on a demographically balanced 402-subject dataset; code available.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address demographic biases and gender-related vascular confounds that hinder finger vein age estimation; correct prior results biased by public datasets.

Method: Multi-instance (three fingers) feature-level fusion with a hybrid fusion approach; multi-task learning optimizing both age regression and gender classification to suppress gender-specific vascular variations.

Result: Mean absolute error of 6.12 years and correlation of 0.880 on 402 subjects; claims to overturn prior consensus about finger vein practicality; code released on GitHub.

Conclusion: Demonstrates viability of finger vein age estimation under debiased data; emphasizes dataset bias as a primary source of past failures.

Abstract: Age estimation from finger vein images has been widely considered impractical due to severe demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors like gender. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE-Vein, a novel multi-instance, multi-task learning framework. Our approach extracts robust structural aging signs by employing a hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers, effectively suppressing local imaging noise. Furthermore, simultaneous optimization of gender classification conditions the network to effectively eliminate gender-specific vascular variations. Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880. Our results not only overturn the conventional consensus regarding the limitations of the finger vein modality but also demonstrate that previous estimation failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsisaoki/MAGE-Vein.

</details>


### [19] [DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20900)
*Pierre Gallin-Martel,Mika Feng,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A lightweight vision-only framework (DINO-VPT) uses hierarchical visual prompt tuning with a Prompt Routing Network (PRN) to adapt prompts to input features, achieving state-of-the-art unified face anti-spoofing performance on UniAttackData without multimodal fusion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Unified FAS models must detect both physical and digital spoofing. Existing VLM-based approaches rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders, adding complexity and potential failure modes. A vision-only solution could simplify architecture and improve generalization.

Method: DINO-VPT adopts hierarchical visual prompt tuning. Prompts are injected dynamically and conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), enabling the model to disentangle diverse spoofing artifacts without any multimodal fusion or text encoders.

Result: On the UniAttackData benchmark, DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods, demonstrating that a well-structured vision-only architecture can reach or surpass multimodal approaches without multimodal supervision.

Conclusion: Vision-only prompt-tuning architectures are effective for unified FAS, reducing reliance on multimodal supervision and external encoders while achieving state-of-the-art performance on challenging benchmarks.

Abstract: With the increasing diversity of spoofing attacks, there is a growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. While existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate high generalization in this context, they heavily rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. In this paper, we propose DINO-VPT, a lightweight, vision-only framework leveraging hierarchical visual prompt tuning. By dynamically injecting prompts conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), our method effectively disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without requiring multimodal fusion. Evaluations on the UniAttackData benchmark demonstrate that DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. Our results indicate that a properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without the need for multimodal supervision.

</details>


### [20] [Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20903)
*Liu Liu,Freya Huying Tan,Fábio Duarte*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Richer visual representations do not always yield more human-aligned judgments of urban engagement; temporally compressed representations (TAIs) match or surpass full video in binary engagement detection, and achieve parity with video in human judgments, while text and audio underperform.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To assess whether increasingly rich representations (spatiotemporal video, TAIs, audio embeddings, text descriptions) yield human-aligned measures of urban engagement, and to understand when temporal compression suffices versus full video encoding.

Method: 1) Spearman correlations between engagement proxies and the four modalities across 61 first-person city-walk videos expanded into 50k ten-second clips; 2) binary high-vs-low engagement classification across multiple classifiers and quantiles; 3) independent 2AFC MTurk study comparing TAIs, full video, text, and audio; 4) gap analysis distinguishing activity-driven vs composition-driven scenes.

Result: Video features show strongest alignment along the temporal-richness continuum in continuous measures (Spearman). However, in binary engagement classification TAIs match or outperform video across classifiers/thresholds. MTurk 2AFC shows participants identify engaging moments with similar accuracy from TAIs and full video; text lags; audio near chance. Gap analysis reveals video excels in dynamic activity scenes, while TAIs excel in composition-driven scenes with stable spatial structure.

Conclusion: Richer representations are not universally more human-aligned. Perceptually grounded temporal compression via TAIs can be a principled alternative to full video encoding for perceptual scoring, with modality suitability depending on scene characteristics.

Abstract: We examine whether richer visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube segmented into over 50,000 ten-second clips and represented across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Spearman correlation analysis reveals the expected ordering along the temporal-richness continuum, with video features showing the strongest continuous alignment. However, this ordering breaks down under binary classification of high- versus low-engagement moments (the paradigm most commonly used to train perceptual scoring models), where TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. An independent two-alternative forced-choice study on Amazon Mechanical Turk confirms that this parity reflects human judgment: participants identified engaging moments with comparable accuracy from TAIs and full video clips, while text performed substantially worse and audio remained near chance. Gap analysis reveals a functional dissociation: video features are advantaged in activity-driven scenes with dynamic content, whereas TAIs better align with human judgments in composition-driven scenes dominated by stable spatial structure. These findings challenge the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned, and suggest that perceptually grounded temporal compression can be a principled alternative to full video encoding.

</details>


### [21] [FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20922)
*Yingdong Hu,Yisheng He,Yiming Jiang,Zehong Lin,Steven Hoi,Jun Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FA-LAM proposes a focus-aware large avatar model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation and 3D/4D reconstruction, addressing attention-related quality bottlenecks with symmetric semantic attention regularization, a dual-phase training pipeline to disentangle reconstruction and animation, and a memory-efficient autoregressive token fusion for multi-view streaming, yielding superior quality at large viewing angles and fine facial regions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome two major limitations in prior SOTA approaches: (1) incorrect/noisy attention activations during 3D head generation and (2) conflicts between reconstruction and animation tasks that degrade cross-domain performance.

Method: 1) Symmetric semantic attention regularization leveraging head symmetry; 2) Dual-phase training that separates large-view reconstruction (hallucination) from animation capabilities into distinct modules; 3) Autoregressive core with visibility-aware token fusion to enable memory-efficient multi-view streaming 4D reconstruction.

Result: Improved reconstruction of animatable Gaussian full heads with higher quality, especially in fine facial regions and at large viewing angles; better integration of 3D and 4D capabilities through modular design and efficient inference.

Conclusion: FA-LAM demonstrates that closing the gap between attention reliability and task disentanglement, plus efficient multi-view processing, yields superior 3D/4D head reconstruction and animation performance.

Abstract: We propose FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery. The core of our method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches. Our analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation. To address the first issue, we introduce a symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy that leverages the inherent semantics and structural symmetry of human heads. To disentangle the objectives of reconstruction and animation, we develop a novel dual-phase training pipeline that separates the model's capabilities for large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. Moreover, we enhance our model to support multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction in an efficient and memory-friendly manner through a core autoregressive modification with tailored visibility-aware token fusion. Collectively, these innovations enable FA-LAM to reconstruct animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, particularly in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

</details>


### [22] [MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20924)
*Ziyi Wang,Siming Zheng,Yang Yang,Shusong Xu,Hao Zhang,Bo Li,Changqing Zou,Peng-Tao Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MagicMakeup introduces a diffusion-transformer framework for region-controllable, high-fidelity makeup transfer that preserves identity. It tackles pixel-to-attention misalignment, coupling of makeup with identity under two-image conditioning, and lack of high-res, region-labeled data by proposing Token-Aligned Region Gating and Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, plus a 1024x1024 data-pair generation pipeline. It shows superior regional controllability, fidelity, and identity preservation across styles, races, and poses.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing diffusion-based makeup transfer suffers from (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment causing spillover and weak regional control, (ii) unclear separation between transfer and preservation under two-image conditioning leading to coupling of makeup attributes with identity, and (iii) absence of a high-resolution, identity-consistent, region-labeled dataset for fine-grained supervision. There is a need for precise region-specific editing, robust identity preservation, and reliable high-res training data.

Method: Diffusion-transformer framework with Token-Aligned Region Gating to align pixel masks with attention and apply region-specific logit gating for precise regional editing while preserving identity. Introduces Cross-Modal Perception Guidance to align text and image features for clearer transfer/preservation concepts. Builds a pipeline to generate 1024x1024 data pairs via region-specific makeup removal, and provides a unified benchmark for synthetic and real settings.

Result: Quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate improved regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation. The method is robust across different styles, races, and poses, indicating strong generalization; a high-resolution 1024x1024 dataset and benchmark are established for fine-grained supervision.

Conclusion: MagicMakeup advances region-controllable makeup transfer with high fidelity and identity preservation by introducing region-aligned gating and cross-modal guidance, supported by a high-resolution data generation pipeline and unified benchmark, showing strong performance and generalization.

Abstract: Makeup-transfer applies the reference makeup to the source face while preserving the source identity. Despite advances in full-face editing by diffusion-based methods, strong regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation remain challenging. The reasons are (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment that causes spillover into non-target areas and weakens regional control; (ii) unclear transfer/preservation concept separation under two-image conditioning, leading to coupling between makeup attributes and identity; and (iii) the lack of a high-resolution dataset that is identity-consistent and region-labeled for fine-grained supervision. In this paper, we propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable and high-fidelity makeup transfer, built on spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. To enable precise region-specific editing while preserving identity, we propose Token-Aligned Region Gating, which aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating. To clarify the concepts of transfer and preservation, we further introduce Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, which aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception. We also design a pipeline for the generation of 1024 x 1024 data pairs through region-specific makeup removal and establish a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MagicMakeup improves regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

</details>


### [23] [Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20940)
*Zekun Li,Xiaoyan Cong,Hongyu Li,Zhiyang Dou,Chuan Guo,Abhay Mittal,Sizhe An,Srinath Sridhar*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Ms.Forcing is a streaming video diffusion framework that uses multi-scale patchification and attention to adapt to per-state noise, reducing tokens and attention compute for real-time generation, and introducing homogeneous-noise-level DMD to align training/inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Enable real-time, long-horizon streaming video generation by overcoming the compute bottlenecks of nested autoregressive and denoising loops in rolling-window diffusion methods.

Method: Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier frames; Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches attention density to query scales; both yield a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD) reuses clean predictions from the same source noise level to reduce DMD training/inference mismatch.

Result: Ms.Forcing achieves 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, with significant improvements in VBench scores for both short and long video generation.

Conclusion: The multi-scale strategy effectively reduces active tokens and attention costs while maintaining stability and quality, enabling practical real-time streaming video diffusion on commodity hardware; H-DMD further mitigates training-inference mismatch.

Abstract: Streaming video diffusion models have made substantial progress toward interactive and dynamic world simulation, but the nested autoregressive and denoising loops of conventional next-frame generation hinder real-time deployment. Recent rolling-window methods pipeline denoising across multiple consecutive frames at different noise levels, improving throughput and long-horizon stability. However, they tokenize every state at the same fine spatial granularity, leaving substantial noise-dependent redundancy in the joint denoising window. We propose Ms.Forcing, an efficient streaming video generation paradigm that adapts spatial granularity to each state's noise level. Its Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier states, reducing the active-window token count by 45%, while Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches the density of visible non-sink keys and values to each query scale to further reduce attention cost. Because both schedules are fixed by window position, Ms.Forcing retains a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. We further introduce Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD), which assembles each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level, thereby reducing the mismatch between DMD training sequences and inference-time rollouts. The multi-scale design helps offset the additional training cost of backpropagating through overlapping windows. We include both quantitative and qualitative experiments to show that Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, while significantly improving VBench scores in both short video and long video generation setting.

</details>


### [24] [FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20955)
*Linke Fan,Xianglong Li,Huixin Huang,Kai Shu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FSB-Net proposes a boundary-aware segmentation framework for NCCT brain stroke lesions using wavelet-based boundary detection, frequency-spatial cross-attention, and spectral boundary loss; it achieves state-of-the-art performance on a public brain stroke CT dataset compared to U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Accurate boundary delineation for NCCT stroke segmentation is hampered by low lesion–brain contrast, heterogeneous ischemic/hemorrhagic morphologies, and partial-volume effects; existing region-overlap losses underrepresent boundary information and can impair precise delineation.

Method: Three components: (i) Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) applying discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features to extract high-frequency boundary representations; (ii) Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) enabling bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for boundary enhancement; (iii) Spectral Boundary Loss enforcing high-frequency consistency in the Fourier domain to sharpen boundaries. The approach uses a PVTv2-B2 encoder and is evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset with ischemic and hemorrhagic cases.

Result: Outperforms baselines (U-Net, UNet++, MANet, DeepLabV3+) on all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95 on the public Brain Stroke CT dataset.

Conclusion: Boundary-aware, frequency-domain segmentation improves boundary sharpness and volumetric accuracy in NCCT brain stroke lesions across subtypes, suggesting broader applicability to boundary-critical medical segmentation and potential impact on clinical decision-making.

Abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain stroke lesions in non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans is critical for rapid clinical decision-making, yet remains difficult due to the low contrast between lesion and normal brain tissue, heterogeneous lesion morphology across ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes, and ambiguous boundaries caused by partial volume effects. Current deep learning approaches primarily optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, leading to imprecise delineation that can affect volumetric assessment and treatment planning. We propose FSB-Net, a frequency-spatial boundary network that leverages frequency-domain analysis for boundary-aware stroke lesion segmentation. FSB-Net introduces three components: (i) a Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) that applies the discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features, extracting high-frequency sub-bands as boundary representations; (ii) a Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) that performs bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for selective boundary enhancement; and (iii) a Spectral Boundary Loss that penalizes high-frequency discrepancies in the Fourier domain to optimize boundary sharpness. Built on a PVTv2-B2 encoder, FSB-Net is evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset containing both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases. Experimental results show that FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance in mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95.

</details>


### [25] [Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction in Dental CBCT using Fine-tuned Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20977)
*G. L. T. Chamika,S. N. A. Dhanapala,P. H. S. V. Nimalaweera,Maheshi B. Dissanayake,Ruwan D. Jayasinghe*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Unsupervised CycleGAN-based MAR for dental CBCT using unpaired ToothFairy data, achieving notable BRISQUE/FID/SSIM gains and real-time performance; recommended for human-in-the-loop use.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Metal artifacts from dental implants severely degrade CBCT, impeding diagnosis. Supervised MAR requires paired voxel-aligned data, which is impractical. An unsupervised CycleGAN leverages unpaired data to restore artifact-free anatomy while preserving morphology.

Method: CycleGAN with U-Net generators and PatchGAN discriminators trained on an unpaired ~4,000-image ToothFairy-derived dataset. Loss functions and architectural choices tuned to reduce generative hallucinations and preserve anatomical integrity. Real-time inference (~3.03 ms per slice). Evaluated on a held-out test set with BRISQUE, FID, and SSIM metrics; expert validation included.

Result: BRISQUE improves by 34.6% (lower is better). FID decreases from 207.03 to 157.04. SSIM achieved 0.9105. Inference time 3.03 ms per slice. Experts report high fidelity; tool recommended as clinical decision-support with human-in-the-loop oversight.

Conclusion: An unsupervised CycleGAN-based MAR framework can deliver high-fidelity artifact reduction in dental CBCT with real-time performance, leveraging unpaired data. It offers robust diagnostic clarity but should be used as a decision-support tool under expert supervision; scalable software pipeline for clinical deployment.

Abstract: Metal artifacts generated by dental implants significantly degrade cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) volumes, obscuring critical anatomical structures and compromising diagnostic precision. To address this, an unsupervised deep learning framework has been proposed for Metal Artifact Reduction (MAR) utilizing a Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) optimized for high-fidelity restoration. Unlike supervised methods that rely on unattainable voxel-aligned paired datasets, the proposed approach leverages an unpaired dataset of approximately 4,000 images, curated from the public ToothFairy dataset. The architecture integrates U-Net-based generators and PatchGAN discriminators, specifically tuned to mitigate generative hallucinations and preserve morphological integrity. Quantitative benchmarking on a held-out test set demonstrates a 34.6\% improvement in the Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) score, a substantial reduction in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) from 207.03 to 157.04, and a superior Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.9105. The framework achieves real-time efficiency with a 3.03 ms inference time per slice, effectively suppressing artifacts while preserving anatomical detail. Expert validation confirms high fidelity; however, to ensure reliability in extreme cases, the architecture is recommended as a clinical decision-support tool under human-in-the-loop oversight. By enhancing diagnostic clarity via a scalable software pipeline, this study provides a robust solution for high-fidelity dental implant imaging.

</details>


### [26] [Distribution-Alignment Bridge for Uncertainty-Aware Text-to-Video Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20984)
*Kyeongmo Chae,Jihoon Lee,Sangtae Ahn*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB) for text-to-video retrieval by modeling text and video as Gaussian distributions and aligning them via a diffusion-inspired bridge using KL-based contrastive loss; reports state-of-the-art results and uncertainty-calibrated rankings.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address uncertainty and misalignment in cross-modal retrieval by moving from point embeddings to probabilistic embeddings, enabling explicit handling of modality-specific uncertainty and distributional transformations.

Method: Represent text and video as Gaussian embeddings (mean, variance). Use a deterministic, diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward their target video distributions through a truncated refinement process. Optimize cross-modal similarity with a distribution-aware contrastive loss based on KL divergence.

Result: Empirically outperforms existing probabilistic and diffusion-based baselines on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX; provides calibrated, uncertainty-aware ranking via bridge-induced distributional margins.

Conclusion: DAB unifies probabilistic embedding and distributional transformation in an end-to-end trainable framework, enabling uncertainty-aware cross-modal retrieval with principled distribution alignment.

Abstract: This paper proposes the Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB), a framework that reconceptualizes text-to-video retrieval as a distribution alignment task rather than traditional deterministic point matching. By modeling both text and video embeddings as Gaussian distributions defined by mean and variance, DAB explicitly accounts for modality-specific uncertainty. We employ a deterministic, diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward their target video distributions through a truncated refinement process. This approach unifies probabilistic embedding and distributional transformation into a cohesive, end-to-end trainable system. To optimize cross-modal similarity, we introduce a distribution-aware contrastive loss based on Kullback-Leibler divergence.
